Three entries in that alphabetical span were skipped, each flagged rather than written silently: "pacific" (a proper adjective derived from a proper noun, the same class Olympic was skipped for on 15/09, §A1 lesson 1); "pc" (an abbreviation with no natural single-word orthographic distractor and a translation that only approximates the headword — "מחשב אישי" — judged not worth the ambiguity this tick); "pence" (a British-currency plural whose one-word Hebrew rendering is genuinely ambiguous with the unrelated word for "face of" — a real translation risk, not a licence or vocabulary problem, deferred rather than guessed per R-010's zero-invention rule).
gate_method: gateSense (lib/core/contentSchema.ts) imported directly and run on every row via a scratch script (.scratch/checkgate.mjs, not pushed) against the full draft set, then re-verified via parseBatchFile on the final .jsonl file through npm run measure:gate — 14/14 pass, 0 rejected. A one-row negative control (Latin letters in translation_he, a duplicated distractor) was run first through the same checker and correctly rejected on both axes (0/1 pass), confirming the checker script itself is wired to the real gate before any real row was trusted. Every non-headword content word in every example and stem was checked against data/generated/allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt with grep -x before the file was finalised (§A1 rule 4); ten first-draft rejections (level drift on cooking/food/social vocabulary not in the NGSL-derived allow-list — bake/baking/baked, loyal, fried, tomato/sauce, hungry, fork/soup/disliked, vacation, ripe/snack, spicy/spicier/sneezed/sprayed, hobby — plus one stem under the 3-word minimum) were caught by the real gate and fixed with allow-listed replacements, then re-verified to 14/14. A separate scripted scan confirmed zero number-words-written-as-text, zero mid-sentence proper nouns, and zero a/an article mismatches directly before a blank across every stem/distractor combination (§A1 lesson 1 and lesson 44).
